summary.title: Web Scraping With Scrapy and MongoDB
summary.one_liner: You learn to set up a Scrapy project, build a spider that extracts book data with CSS selectors, and store the results in MongoDB through an item pipeline.
takeaways: Create a Scrapy project with startproject and generate a spider with genspider.
Use the Scrapy shell to test CSS selectors before writing spider code.
Define an Item subclass with fields such as url, title and price, then yield items from parse().
Frame scraping as ETL: spider extracts, item pipeline transforms and loads into MongoDB.
summary.summary: This Real Python tutorial walks through building a web scraper with Scrapy and storing the results in MongoDB. It starts by installing Scrapy and creating a project for the Books to Scrape site, then inspects the page structure with browser developer tools. The Scrapy shell is used to test CSS selectors for book titles, URLs and prices before they are placed in a BooksItem and used in a spider's parse method. The part of the page provided ends before the data-extraction run and the MongoDB pipeline are covered.
